whoIsThisFor.heading: Who should take the Contact Center AP exam?

personas.label: Service Cloud implementers
personas.description: You set up Omni-Channel routing, voice, or digital channels and want to prove your contact center skills.

personas.label: Contact center managers
personas.description: You lead an agent team and want to understand how work is routed and measured.

personas.label: Partners delivering contact center projects
personas.description: You build Service Cloud Voice, messaging, and bot solutions for clients.

examDifficulty.heading: Is the Contact Center AP exam hard?
examDifficulty.summary: This exam focuses on how work reaches agents and how agents handle it. Routing is the largest topic, followed by voice, bots, and digital channels.
bullets: 60 scored questions in 75 minutes, plus up to five unscored questions that do not count.
66% to pass, which is 40 correct answers out of 60.
Routing matters: Study queues, skills, capacity, presence statuses, and Omni-Channel Flows.
Know the channels: Prepare for Service Cloud Voice, messaging, bots, and knowledge-based self-service.
examDifficulty.passRateGuidance: Hands-on work with Omni-Channel and at least one voice or messaging channel helps. Aim for 80% or higher on timed practice tests before booking.

examFormat.heading: Contact Center AP exam format
examFormat.intro: Accredited Professional exams are taken online. Here is what to expect:
examFormat.scenarioPercent: Questions often describe a contact center problem, such as calls reaching the wrong team or agents receiving too many chats. Choose the setting that fixes it.
bestWayToPass: Choose a routing method: Know when to use queues, skills, or attributes to match work with agents.
Set agent capacity: Learn how capacity and work item size affect the amount of work each agent receives.
Understand voice setup: Know how Service Cloud Voice, Amazon Connect or a partner telephony provider, and IVR fit together.
Design self-service: Use bots and knowledge articles to answer common questions before they reach an agent.

certificationCard.description: This exam tests how to set up a Service Cloud contact center, including agent routing, voice and digital channels, bots, knowledge, and reporting. It has 60 scored questions in 75 minutes and a 66% passing score.

keyConcepts.h2: Contact Center AP: Key Concepts for the Exam

blocks.heading: Omni-Channel Routing & Queues
blocks.body: **Omni-Channel** routes cases, chats, calls, and other work to available agents. **Queue-based routing** offers work to available members of a queue. **Skills-based routing** matches work to agents with the right skills, such as a language or product. **Omni-Channel Flows** can use logic, such as sending VIP customers to a specialist team. **Routing configurations** set priority and how much capacity each work item uses. Agents choose a **presence status** to show which types of work they can take.

blocks.heading: Service Cloud Voice & CTI Integration
blocks.body: **Service Cloud Voice** brings phone calls into the Service Console alongside the customer record and transcript. It can use **Amazon Connect** or a partner telephony provider. Calls can be routed through Omni-Channel with other work. The **IVR** (phone menu) and contact flows are set up in the telephony system, which can look up Salesforce data. Real-time transcription can help supervisors follow calls and can support AI suggestions.

blocks.heading: Einstein Bots & Digital Engagement
blocks.body: Customers can contact a business through **messaging** such as web chat, in-app messaging, SMS, and WhatsApp. **Bots**, including Einstein Bots and Agentforce agents, can answer common questions, collect details, and hand a conversation to a person. Pass the conversation and details to the agent so the customer does not have to repeat them. Omni-Channel can route messaging sessions as it routes cases and calls.

blocks.heading: Knowledge Management & Deflection
blocks.body: Knowledge articles can support several contact-center channels: agents search for and attach answers to cases, help sites publish self-service content, and bots can suggest articles during chat. When the customer resolves an issue without agent help, the contact center records a deflected interaction. Keep article publishing and audience visibility in mind when planning which answers each channel can surface.

blocks.heading: Reporting & Contact Center Analytics
blocks.body: **Omni Supervisor** lets supervisors monitor queues, agent status, and wait times in real time, and reassign work. Reports and dashboards can show average handle time, first contact resolution, wait time, abandonment rate, and customer satisfaction. Use these measures to review staffing, routing, and bot content.

scenarioTips.h2: How to pass the Contact Center AP exam
scenarioTips.intro: Many questions ask how to get the right work to the right agent at the right time. Check skills, capacity, and priority before choosing a setting.

blocks.heading: Service Cloud Voice Architecture
blocks.body: Voice uses Amazon Connect or a partner provider. The phone menu is set up in the telephony system, while agents handle calls in the Service Console.

blocks.heading: Omni-Channel Routing for Contact Center
blocks.body: Use queues for straightforward routing, skills when agents have different abilities, and Omni-Channel Flows when routing needs decision logic.

blocks.heading: IVR Design & Self-Service
blocks.body: Use an IVR to identify the caller and reason for calling, then route the call. Offer self-service for simple requests.

blocks.heading: Agent Experience Configuration
blocks.body: Macros, Quick Text, and Knowledge can help agents resolve cases faster in the Service Console.

blocks.heading: Reporting & Analytics
blocks.body: Use Omni Supervisor for live queues and agent status. Reports help track handle time, wait time, resolution, and satisfaction.

nextCertsAfter.intro: Good next steps after Contact Center:

sampleQuestions.question: Spanish-speaking customers are reaching agents who speak only English. Which routing method can fix this?
options: Queue-based routing to a shared team
sampleQuestions.explanation: Skills-based routing sends work only to agents with the needed skill, such as speaking Spanish.
whyWrong: Priority changes the order of work, not which agents receive it.
More capacity does not match customers with the right language skill.

sampleQuestions.question: Agents receive too many chats at once and response times are getting worse. What should the admin adjust?
options: The IVR menu and phone options
sampleQuestions.explanation: Capacity settings control how much work an agent can receive at once. Adjust the capacity and the amount each chat uses.
whyWrong: The IVR handles phone calls, not chats.
Page layouts do not control routing.
Email routing settings do not control chat capacity.

sampleQuestions.question: VIP customers should go to a senior team while other customers use normal routing. What is the most flexible setup?
options: A Knowledge article for VIP customers
sampleQuestions.explanation: An Omni-Channel Flow can check customer details, such as VIP status, and route the work based on that information.
whyWrong: Knowledge articles provide information; they do not route work.
Manual assignment is slow and may be inconsistent.
A separate org is more than this routing need requires.

sampleQuestions.question: Agents need the phone call, customer record, and live transcript together in the Service Console. What provides this?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Service Cloud Voice brings calls into the Service Console with customer information and transcription.
whyWrong: Email-to-Case handles email messages.
Web-to-Lead captures leads from a website form.

sampleQuestions.question: When using Service Cloud Voice with Amazon Connect, where is the “press 1 for billing” phone menu usually built?
sampleQuestions.explanation: The IVR and contact flows are set up in the telephony system. They can use Salesforce data to help route calls.
whyWrong: Knowledge articles provide answers, not phone menus.
Page layouts arrange record pages.
Validation Rules check record data when users save it.

sampleQuestions.question: Customers ask the same simple delivery question many times. What can reduce chats about it?
sampleQuestions.explanation: A bot can answer common questions with Knowledge and hand the conversation to an agent when needed.
whyWrong: Lower priority delays a response but does not answer the question.
Removing chat makes it harder for customers to get help.
More agents may handle the volume but do not reduce repeated questions.

sampleQuestions.question: When a bot transfers a chat to an agent, what information should it pass along?
options: Bot setup link and configuration notes
Customer name and chosen topic only
Pass the chat and collected details
A fresh chat with no prior messages
sampleQuestions.explanation: Passing the conversation and collected details helps the agent continue without asking the customer to repeat information.
whyWrong: A name alone may not give the agent enough context.
Starting over makes the customer repeat what they already told the bot.

sampleQuestions.question: A supervisor wants to see live agent status and customer wait times. Which tool should they use?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Omni Supervisor shows queue and agent status in real time and lets supervisors reassign work.
whyWrong: Setup Audit Trail records configuration changes.
A monthly report is not a live view.
Data Loader moves records in bulk.

sampleQuestions.question: An agent should be available for chats but not phone calls. What should they do?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Presence statuses tell Omni-Channel which kinds of work an agent can receive.
whyWrong: Closing the console would stop the agent from handling work there.
A profile controls permissions, not live availability.

sampleQuestions.question: Agents send the same password-reset reply many times each day. What can save time?
options: Set up a new IVR menu
sampleQuestions.explanation: Quick Text inserts a saved response. A Macro can run several steps at once.
whyWrong: An IVR menu is for phone calls.
Capacity controls how much work agents receive.
A queue routes work; it does not provide a saved reply.

sampleQuestions.question: Which measure shows how often customers leave before an agent answers?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Abandonment rate measures contacts that end before an agent answers.
whyWrong: First Contact Resolution measures issues solved on the first contact.
Article count is not a contact outcome measure.
Average handle time measures how long an agent spends on a contact.

sampleQuestions.question: Customers want to use WhatsApp and have their conversations handled by Salesforce agents. What should be set up?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Messaging supports channels such as WhatsApp, and Omni-Channel can route sessions to agents.
whyWrong: Web-to-Case creates cases from a website form.
Email-to-Case handles email requests.
A Knowledge site can provide information but does not handle a live conversation.

sampleQuestions.question: A Knowledge article should be available to agents but hidden from customers on the help site. How should this be controlled?
options: Move the article to a separate org
sampleQuestions.explanation: Knowledge visibility settings control which audiences can see an article, including internal users and the public.
whyWrong: Deleting the article also removes it for agents.
A separate org is unnecessary for controlling article visibility.

sampleQuestions.question: Urgent cases should be offered before normal cases in the same queue. What should the admin set?
options: Make the Case description field longer
Add more agents to the queue
sampleQuestions.explanation: Routing priority determines which work is offered first.
whyWrong: Description length does not affect routing.
More agents change capacity, not the order of work.
Page layouts do not set routing order.

sampleQuestions.question: A manager wants to measure how many issues are solved during the customer’s first contact. Which measure fits?
options: Average time before an agent answers
sampleQuestions.explanation: First Contact Resolution shows the share of issues solved without a follow-up contact.
whyWrong: Speed to answer measures wait time.
Abandonment rate tracks customers who leave before an agent responds.
Utilization measures how busy agents are.
